module: Make and maintain the deployment decision

lesson.title: Special route: remote biometric identification
lesson.summary: Optional specialist route: authorisation, human verification and biometric records.

prerequisites.reason: This is a special human-oversight measure.

blocks: **Remote biometric identification** identifies people without their active involvement, typically at a distance, by comparing biometric data with a reference database. Biometric data concerns physical/physiological/behavioural characteristics used for identification. Post-remote identification is delayed identification rather than the real-time form.

This optional lesson does not authorise a real biometric use. First check scope, Article 5, data law and the exact Annex III point; confirm national rules. The supplied exercise assumes a legally permitted targeted post-remote investigation route subject to the stated controls.

For the specified targeted search of a suspect or convicted person, Article 26(10) requests judicial or binding, judicially reviewable administrative authorisation in advance or without undue delay and no later than 48 hours. The narrow initial-identification exception uses objective/verifiable facts directly linked to the offence.

Limit use to what is strictly necessary for the specific criminal investigation. Rejected authorisation requires immediately stopping the linked use and deleting linked personal data. Untargeted law-enforcement use is barred; no adverse legal decision may rest solely on the output. Data-law and stricter national rules remain.

**Biometric dual verification** under 14(5) requires identification from Annex III 1(a) systems to be separately verified and confirmed by at least two competent, trained and authorised natural persons before the deployer acts on it.

The qualified exception concerns law enforcement, migration, border control or asylum where Union/national law considers dual verification disproportionate. Sector membership alone does not establish the exception.

**Biometric log fields** under 12(3) include each use’s start/end date and time, reference database, matched input data, and the identity of verifying natural persons. This system capability differs from custody periods and operational police records.

Article 26(10) also requires each use in the relevant police file regardless of purpose/deployer, authority availability on request, and annual reports to market-surveillance and data-protection authorities; sensitive law-enforcement operational-data qualifications apply. Reports may aggregate deployments.

Case: a permitted targeted search has authorisation refused; the team proposes continuing because one person approved a match. Stop the linked use and delete linked data. Neither a match nor internal approval overrides refusal.
Record the national-law verification rather than inventing a universal approving office. This extension has no core-course lesson depending on it.

questions.prompt: Authorisation for the specified linked post-remote use is rejected. What follows?

options.blocks: Immediately stop linked use and delete linked personal data
options.reason: The refusal clause expressly requires these actions.

options.blocks: Continue until the annual report is due
Continue if one staff member agrees
options.reason: Internal agreement is not the requested authorisation.
